Phase: Specification. Using the documentation skill, create the final three spec files. No code.
Read spec/requirements.md, spec/state-machine.md, spec/data-model.md and

1) spec/api-contract.md
   Endpoints (base /api/v1), each with: FR IDs, request, response, status codes, example JSON:
   - POST   /tickets                 → 201 + Location, full ticket detail (comments: [])
   - GET    /tickets?q=&status=&page=&size=&sort=  → 200 paginated summaries
            (single endpoint for list, search and filter; no separate search endpoint)
   - GET    /tickets/{id}            → 200 ticket detail
   - PATCH  /tickets/{id}            → 200 ticket detail (partial update; version required)
   - PATCH  /tickets/{id}/status     → 200 ticket detail; body {status, version}
   - POST   /tickets/{id}/comments   → 201 created comment
   Define:
   - TicketSummary (id, title, status, priority, assignee, createdAt, updatedAt, version)
   - TicketDetail (summary fields + description, comments[] ascending, allowedTransitions[]
     computed by the backend from state-machine.md)
   - Comment (id, author, body, createdAt)
   - Our own page response DTO: content, page, size, totalElements, totalPages
     (do not serialise Spring's Page directly)
   - Sort whitelist: createdAt, updatedAt, title with asc/desc; default createdAt,desc;
     anything else → 400
   - Problem Details (RFC 7807) with type URIs: /problems/validation-error (400, with
     errors[{field, message}]), /problems/not-found (404), /problems/stale-version (409),
     /problems/invalid-transition (409), /problems/terminal-ticket (409),
     /problems/internal-error (500, no stack traces or internals)
   - Check order from requirements; Common request rules (unknown fields → 400 etc.)
   - Note springdoc-openapi will generate the live spec at /v3/api-docs and /swagger-ui.html;
     this document is the source of truth and the generated one must match it
   - Traceability table: endpoint → FR/NFR IDs

2) spec/ui-flow.md
   - Routes: /tickets (list), /tickets/new, /tickets/:id (detail)
   - Mermaid navigation flow
   - Per screen: components, data loaded, user actions, API calls, loading/empty/error states
     - List: search box (debounced), status filter dropdown, pagination, "New ticket" button
     - Create: form with client-side hints but backend as validation authority; on success go
       to detail page (FR-12-AC1)
     - Detail: editable fields form (sends version), status buttons rendered from
       allowedTransitions, comments list + add comment form; terminal tickets show fields and
       status actions disabled, comments still enabled
   - Error display mapping per Problem Details type: validation → messages under fields;
     not-found → "Ticket not found" page with link back; stale-version → banner with
     "Reload" action; invalid-transition and terminal-ticket → banner with backend detail;
     network/500 → generic retry message
   - Trace each screen/behaviour to FR-12 ACs

3) spec/test-strategy.md
   - Test pyramid and tools per layer, following .cursor/rules/testing.mdc
   - Backend:
     - Unit: TicketStatus

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
Cross-referencing requirements against the API contract reveals a mismatch. CRR-01 specifies non-numeric path IDs return 400. The API contract defines path IDs as positive integers.

The CRR-01 requirement leaves edge cases ambiguous. It does not explicitly reject zero, negative values, or very large numbers.

FR-01-AC1 and the API contract both specify full tickets. The API contract adds allowedTransitions and comments[]. This is enrichment rather than a contradiction. The data model aligns with the response format.

State-machine.md and the API contract disagree on stale-version rejection order. The state machine rejects stale versions before evaluating transition rules. Decision 13 orders stale checks before invalid transition checks. Terminal ticket PATCH correctly rejects stale versions before terminal edits. A stale version on a terminal ticket returns 409 stale. A current version on a terminal ticket returns 409 invalid transition. A stale version on CLOSED returns 409 stale. A current version on CLOSED returns 409 invalid transition.

The architecture sequence diagram contradicts the API contract. It shows POST transition while the contract uses PATCH /tickets/{id}/status. api-standards.mdc aligns with the PATCH approach.

FR-11 covers stale versions on PATCH and transition. Comments lack versions, so stale checks do not apply there. Concurrent PATCH conflicts are handled by the architecture through OptimisticLockException returning 409 stale.

FR-03 lacks an acceptance criterion for `allowedTransitions`. FR-12-AC8 consumes this field, yet requirements never define it.

FR-08 omits acceptance criteria for invalid sort fields and for sorting by updatedAt or title. This creates a testability gap.

FR-06 keyword search implies OR semantics across title and description. The API contract does not explicitly state this. It could be interpreted as AND instead.

FR-04-AC5 covers empty assignee on PATCH.

POST comment returns 201 with an optional Location header. This weakens REST consistency.

Malicious JSON Content-Type handling is not specified.

FR-05-AC3 rejects empty comment bodies. It does not address whitespace-only bodies. This leaves a gap for comment validation.

FR-08-AC4 correctly returns zero totalElements and totalPages for empty result sets. When a page exceeds the final available page, the API contract returns an empty content array. totalPages should be derived from totalElements. The data model TicketSummary includes version. NFR-02-AC2 references the API contract.

The UI flow documentation does not clarify whether clients validate non-numeric IDs before routing or rely on API error responses.

A value of 0 raises a critical ambiguity. It could be rejected as non-numeric under CRR-01, or treated as a valid but missing ticket ID under CRR-02.

Concurrent comment creation and PATCH operations are handled safely. Comments do not alter ticket versions, so multiple comment submissions can succeed independently.

FR-09 acceptance criteria omit an explicit requirement that transition success returns a full ticket body. The API contract resolves this, but the traceability table may not reflect it.

Several error scenarios are missing from the API contract. These include wrong Content-Type on POST and PATCH, duplicate query parameters on GET list, empty PATCH bodies, and missing status fields during transitions.

Architecture document line 208 still cites api-contract.md for endpoint and Problem Details URI details. That reference is outdated because those details are now resolved in the API contract itself.

FR-05-AC2 leaves whitespace-only comment authors ambiguous. The UI hardcodes sort=createdAt,desc and does not allow users to change it. This is acceptable because the requirements do not mandate a configurable sort.

NFR-02 omits an explicit acceptance criterion for the shape of 500 internal-error responses. The API contract defines this shape, but the requirement does not.

The test strategy does not explicitly call out integration tests for decision 13 check order.

The API contract’s CRR-03 PATCH forbidden fields list is incomplete. It omits comments, allowedTransitions, and id from the forbidden set.

Empty request bodies on PATCH are not specified.

FR-03-AC1 does not explicitly require allowedTransitions. The API contract adds this field to full ticket responses. FR-01 implies that full tickets contain description. The data model includes description. This is a minor contradiction.

Medium severity issues include ambiguous search OR semantics, path ID zero and negative rules, and missing custom sort acceptance criteria. Low severity issues include stale
</details></think>

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
FR-11 omits the OptimisticLockException race condition. The architecture covers it, but requirements lack acceptance criteria. FR-11-AC3 for JPA concurrent save is missing. Requirements alone cannot test this without architecture.

Decision 13 correctly prioritizes 409 over 404 for stale PATCHes and missing tickets. Empty PATCH bodies return 400 per FR-04-AC7 and FR-04-AC9. FR-03 lacks acceptance criteria for allowedTransitions, though FR-12-AC8 depends on it. NFR-07 contradicts itself by requiring POST transitions in the state machine.

FR-07 does not specify whether an empty status string is invalid. This leaves ambiguity between omitted and empty filters. Duplicate sort parameters are also unspecified. FR-09 lacks acceptance criteria for updating allowedTransitions in the success response.

NFR-07 matrix tests correctly expect 409 for invalid transitions after version synchronization. Integration matrix tests for terminal states also require current versions. The test strategy omits an explicit WebMvcTest case verifying that stale versions take precedence over terminal ticket checks under Decision 13.

CRR-01 and the API contract disagree on what counts as a non-numeric version. Zero, negative numbers, decimals, and leading zeros are ambiguous.

JavaScript BigInt precision for very large JSON version numbers is a low-priority edge case.

FR-05-AC2 cites CRR-04 for invalid authors, yet this only applies when the ticket exists. There is no acceptance criterion for comments on missing tickets with invalid bodies. PATCH requests to missing tickets with invalid JSON should return 404 first. This is a spec clarity issue worth Medium severity for test expectations. The state machine correctly treats a stale version as an invalid transition from CLOSED rather than a stale check. The omission may be intentional to prevent leaking validation errors, or it may be an oversight.
</details></think>
